generation.explanation: The law of cosines generalizes the Pythagorean theorem to any triangle: c² = a² + b² − 2ab cos(C). When angle C is 90°, cos(C) = 0 so the correction term vanishes and you recover a² + b² = c². For acute angles the correction is negative (c is shorter than the right-triangle case); for obtuse angles cos(C) < 0 so the term becomes positive and c is longer.
